title: Shortness of Breath
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset dyspnea, tachypnea, hypoxemia, petechial rash (chest, axillae, conjunctivae), and CNS changes (confusion, AMS) 24-72 hours after a long bone fracture (femur, tibia) or pelvic fracture. Fat embolism syndrome is caused by fat globules from bone marrow entering venous circulation → lodged in pulmonary and cerebral capillaries → mechanical obstruction + inflammatory cascade. Triad: respiratory distress + petechial rash + CNS dysfunction. Diagnosis is clinical (no gold standard test). CXR may show diffuse bilateral infiltrates (ARDS pattern). ABG: hypoxemia, A-a gradient elevated. UA may show fat globules in urine. Treatment: SUPPORTIVE — oxygen, respiratory support (may require mechanical ventilation). Early surgical fixation of long bone fractures reduces risk. Maintain adequate oxygenation and hemodynamics.
chief_complaint: Acute dyspnea, petechial rash post long bone fracture
